studies.title: Nocardiosis in the COVID-19 Era: A Narrative Review of Pathogenesis, Clinical Challenges, and the Gut-Lung Axis.
studies.authors: Ghazanfari Jajin, Morteza, Fateh, Abolfazl
studies.abstract: The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic has increased susceptibility to secondary opportunistic infections, including nocardiosis. Nocardia species, uncommon but potentially fatal bacteria, primarily affect immunocompromised hosts through inhalation or direct inoculation, causing pulmonary, disseminated, and central nervous system (CNS) disease. This review examines severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2)-induced immune dysregulation, iatrogenic immunosuppression from corticosteroids and immunomodulators, and host vulnerabilities in COVID-19-associated nocardiosis. Emerging data highlight demographic shifts, pathophysiological mechanisms, clinical presentations, diagnostic challenges, treatment strategies, and prognostic outcomes. Pulmonary involvement is most common, but CNS abscesses drive substantial mortality. Cutaneous involvement is uncommon but has been reported. Nonspecific clinical and radiologic features, slow microbial growth, and masking by empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics complicate timely diagnosis. Advanced molecular diagnostics, including metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) and matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS), may facilitate earlier detection. Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole remains the cornerstone of prolonged, often combination antimicrobial therapy, guided by species identification and susceptibility testing, with linezolid, carbapenems, and amikacin as key alternatives. Although human data are limited, the gut-lung axis is increasingly recognized as influencing systemic immunity and host susceptibility to Nocardia. This rare but emerging co-infection underscores the need for clinical vigilance, prompt diagnosis, and individualized, multidisciplinary management. Further studies are warranted to determine incidence, optimize diagnostic approaches, and clarify molecular interactions between viral and bacterial pathogens post-COVID-19.

studies.title: Alcohol consumption prior to SARS-CoV-2 infection and Long COVID: A retrospective analysis by alcoholic beverage type and intake level.
studies.authors: Torres-Romero, Maria Gabriela, Escrivá, Nicolás, Barado, Elena, Moreno-Galarraga, Laura et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID (LC) is a post-acute condition persisting after a SARS-CoV-2 infection. Evidence on alcohol consumption in LC is limited. This study evaluated the association between pre-infection alcohol consumption and LC by intake level and beverage type. This retrospective case-control study (May 2022-June 2025) included 340 adults with confirmed COVID-19. LC was defined based on the World Health Organization's definition using questionnaire data. Alcohol consumption was quantified as grams of ethanol/day. Beverage-specific analyses were performed. Multivariable logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Of the 340 participants, 202 (59.4%) met the definition of LC. Compared with abstainers, moderate (OR = 0.44; 95% CI: 0.23-0.82) and high alcohol consumption (OR = 0.35; 95% CI: 0.12-0.99) were inversely associated with LC in the fully adjusted model. Each additional gram of ethanol/day was associated with lower odds of LC (OR = 0.94; 95% CI: 0.90-0.99). Beer and liquor consumption showed inverse associations, although the liquor estimate was based on few exposed LC cases. Pre-infection alcohol consumption was inversely associated with LC, including moderate and high intake categories, but these observational findings do not establish a causal or protective effect. Further studies are needed.

studies.title: Affinity Capture-Migration/Separation Technologies for Investigating Post-Acute SARS-CoV-2 Persistence and Candidate Biomarkers of Long COVID.
studies.authors: Guzman, Norberto A, Berck, Clifford M, Krylov, Sergey N
studies.abstract: The management of COVID-19 continues to evolve as clinical experience and scientific research refine approaches to diagnosis, isolation protocols, and treatment. Diagnosing COVID-19 relies on either molecular tests to detect specific viral genetic material or antigen tests to detect viral proteins. Molecular tests generally have higher analytical sensitivity and accuracy than antigen tests, particularly early in infection. The SARS-CoV-2 RNA genetic material may remain detectable for prolonged periods after infection. Immunoassay antigen tests detect specific viral proteins but are less sensitive than molecular tests and can miss early infection. Laboratory diagnosis of acute COVID-19 commonly relies on molecular or antigen testing of respiratory specimens, including nasopharyngeal or other appropriate specimens. Both molecular and antigen tests may yield false-negative results due to insufficient viral load in the nasopharynx or false-positive results caused by sample contamination or cross-reactivity. Sputum can provide a complementary respiratory specimen, particularly in patients with productive cough; reported detection advantages depend on the sampling time, comparator specimen and assay. Pretreatment of sputum with surfactants and proteolytic enzymes effectively breaks down the sample to release viral antigens. Its effects on antigen recovery and assay interference require validation for the selected target and test. Prolonged detection of viral components has been reported, but their detection does not establish replication-competent virus. This preparation method is simple and uses small sample volumes. This narrative review explores how affinity capture-migration and affinity capture-separation techniques could use sputum and other biological fluid samples to investigate the long-term effects of COVID-19, which can lead to long-lasting multi-organ issues, as well as the impact of quantifying pro-inflammatory cytokines and aberrant glycoproteins in the lingering inflammation after COVID-19 infection. A search was conducted in Google, PubMed (MEDLINE), and Web of Science, using sputum proteomics, immunoassay testing, affinity capture-separation techniques, aberrant glycans, pro-inflammatory cytokines, COVID-19 and Long COVID as keywords, primarily selecting the most referenced and related papers of the last decade. Because post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 can afflict any individual post-infection-including pediatric populations-advancing robust analytical platforms like affinity capture-separation is vital for clearer diagnostic resolution. This narrative review article underscores the critical need for diagnostic techniques that transcend the limitations of traditional rapid antigen and molecular tests for COVID-19 and Long COVID. We highlight affinity capture-separation techniques as a promising complementary approach. Affinity capture-separation can enrich and resolve selected cytokines, proteins, glycoproteins and glycans. Its application to candidate Long COVID biomarkers is promising but is not a clinically validated diagnostic use. If validated, these platforms could offer a more comprehensive approach to evaluating systemic inflammation in severe COVID-19 and Long COVID patients.

studies.title: Long-Term Cardiopulmonary Sequelae and Rehabilitation After MERS-CoV and COVID-19: A Narrative Review from a Saudi Perspective.
studies.authors: Alruwaili, Rawan, Albelasi, Abdullah, Alqahtani, Mohammed M
studies.abstract: Saudi Arabia has carried the largest global burden of Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV) and a substantial burden of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), the cause of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). This narrative review, written from the perspectives of clinical immunology and cardiopulmonary rehabilitation, synthesises evidence on long-term sequelae (persisting for at least 3 months) and rehabilitation after MERS-CoV infection and COVID-19, with implications for Saudi Arabia. MERS-CoV survivors show reduced diffusing capacity for at least 12 months, radiographic lung fibrosis in about one-third of recovering patients at short-term follow-up, and high rates of chronic fatigue, depression and post-traumatic stress. A dedicated search of six databases and registries (355 records) found no study of a rehabilitation intervention after MERS-CoV infection. Because most MERS-CoV survivors with sequelae were critically ill, evidence on post-intensive care syndrome and acute respiratory distress syndrome is the closest basis for extrapolation; it shows persistent disability but uncertain benefit from generic post-discharge programmes. After COVID-19, randomised trials show that rehabilitation improves functional capacity, dyspnoea and quality of life, while post-exertional malaise, autonomic dysfunction and myocardial involvement require screening and symptom-titrated or cardiology-guided care. We propose a phenotype-directed rehabilitation pathway with explicit screening criteria, adapted to Saudi factors that include Vision 2030 reforms and virtual care, high metabolic comorbidity, a hot climate, women's access to physical activity and occupational groups at risk of MERS-CoV, and a research agenda that includes MERS-CoV survivor registries and rehabilitation trials.

studies.title: The Long COVID Care Pathway in France: A Patient Journey Map Toward Social Downgrading.
studies.authors: Dumesnil, Hélène, Oustric, Pauline, Cossalter, Claude-Odile, Delahaye-Grélois, Séverine et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID, which can significantly impair patients' functional abilities and quality of life, affects an estimated 2.1 million people in France. Better understanding of how affected individuals navigate the health-care system over time is required to adapt care to their needs. This study aimed to map care trajectories in France from the patients' perspectives. We conducted a qualitative study among 33 adults with long COVID, as part of a participatory research project involving a patient organization. Semi-structured interviews were analyzed by thematic inductive and patient journey mapping approaches. We identified six key stages in these trajectories, ranging from the onset of unexplained symptoms to learning to live differently. The pathway often began with a general practitioner's dismissal or minimization of their symptoms. Diagnostic delay followed. Diagnosis was frequently patient-initiated and further prolonged by geographical inequalities in specialist access; for some, it remained unattained despite embodied certainty. Multiple issues accumulated, each potentiating the others throughout the pathway, resulting in progressive social decline. This process was not simply a consequence of the disease itself but was actively produced and amplified by failures at every level of the health-care and social-insurance systems. Findings suggest that long COVID care pathways can actively contribute to, rather than prevent, social downgrading, which thus appears to be a care-induced social trajectory. These results call for longitudinal research among underrepresented groups, alongside concrete action: improved training for clinicians and social insurance practitioners, better-coordinated referral pathways, and structural reform of the health-care-social insurance interface.

studies.title: Cognitive and Mood Symptoms Associated with Unemployment in Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19.
studies.journal: Journal of occupational and environmental medicine
studies.authors: Reynolds, W Cody, Abril, Isabel, Ortiz-Acosta, Perla, Becker, Jacqueline H et al.
studies.abstract: To examine whether subjective and objective cognitive function, mood, and fatigue are associated with unemployment in individuals with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC). In this cross-sectional study, 66 individuals with PASC (meanage=46.35) completed self-report measures of fatigue, depression, anxiety, and subjective cognitive decline, and neuropsychological testing. Participants had COVID-19 ≥ 2 months prior, brain fog, at least two other persistent symptoms with no major or unstable neurological or psychiatric disorder, and were not hospitalized during infection. Analysis of covariance was conducted, controlling for demographics, mood, and fatigue. Unemployed participants (29%) reported greater perceived executive dysfunction since COVID-19 and exhibited poorer performance on measures of immediate memory and working memory compared to employed participants. Unemployed individuals with PASC demonstrate greater cognitive difficulties, highlighting the need for optimized symptom management in this population.

studies.title: Prevalence, Changes, and Factors Associated with Long COVID in Mainland China after the Policy Shift: Findings from a Two-Wave Cross-Sectional Study.
studies.journal: Journal of epidemiology and global health
studies.authors: Ruan, Xiaoli, Yuan, Yang, Wang, Yujie, Zhang, Yujing et al.
studies.abstract: The long-term consequences of the Chinese COVID-19 wave in 2022 remain unknown. Therefore, this study aimed to clarify the long COVID symptoms of COVID-19 survivors after the wave of Omicron in 2022 and to reveal related factors of sequelae symptoms. A repeated cross-sectional survey design was employed, comprising two survey waves conducted in August 2023 and August 2024 among the general population in mainland China. Participants completed an online questionnaire for evaluation of symptoms and characteristics. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression were used to identify factors associated with long COVID. A total of 47,464 participants were included. The overall prevalence of long COVID was 52.34%, showing a gradual decline over time, with fatigue being the most prevalent symptom. All estimates were reported as odds ratio (95% confidence interval). Factors positively associated with long COVID included female gender (1.17 [1.12-1.22]), aged 18-59 (1.21 [1.11-1.32]), having any chronic diseases (2.19 [2.07-2.31]) or mental disorders (2.98 [2.85-3.11]) and drinking (1.23 [1.17-1.29]). Conversely, maintaining a regular sleep-wake (0.81 [0.77-0.84]), combining meat and vegetable diets (0.83 [0.78-0.87]), consuming vegetables (0.83 [0.79-0.88]), dairy products (0.91 [0.85-0.98]), and animal foods daily (0.91 [0.86-0.96]), sunbathing at least 5 h per day (0.93 [0.89-0.98]), having a satisfactory neighborhood relationship (0.81 [0.75-0.87]) and community environment (0.71 [0.66-0.75]) and vaccination (2 doses: 0.85 [0.77-0.93]; 3 doses: 0.87 [0.79-0.95]; ≥4 doses: 0.81 [0.70-0.93]) demonstrated significant inverse associations with long COVID. Long COVID remains one of the major health challenges and is influenced by a variety of factors. As such, the targeted monitoring, identification, and management of at-risk populations guided by these associated factors carry substantialis public health significance. Community-based programs promoting nutrition and sleep hygiene, combined with sustained vaccination, could help reduce the burden of long COVID. Furthermore, integrating screening and management into routine primary care for high-risk groups, alongside a national surveillance system, represents an actionable policy direction.

studies.title: Clinical Characteristics and Invasive Management of Acute Myocardial Infarction in the Post-COVID-19 Era.
studies.journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
studies.authors: Bobrowska, Beata, Zdzierak, Barbara, Krawczyk-Ożóg, Agata, Skowron, Kamil et al.
studies.abstract: Organizing healthcare delivery during an epidemic is a major challenge that reshapes patient experience and can have lasting effects on perceptions of care and on the healthcare system's structure and function. The study analyzed how the COVID-19 pandemic altered the profile of myocardial infarction (MI) patients treated at the University Hospital in Krakow. Data on diagnostic and interventional procedures performed in patients with MI were collected from February 2018 to July 2024 and divided into three equal periods: before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Risk factors were interview-based and not validated against laboratory data. Of 2703 procedures, 855 were pre-COVID (31.63%), 842 during COVID (31.15%) and 1006 post-COVID (37.22%). During COVID, NSTEMI increased relative to STEMI ( In the immediate post-pandemic period, myocardial infarction (MI) hospitalizations increased by about 20% compared with the pandemic phase, along with a proportional rise in diagnostic and therapeutic invasive procedures, despite a lower documented prevalence of traditional coronary artery disease risk factors in the post-pandemic cohort.

studies.title: Clinical Utility and Limitations of Sub-Basal Corneal Nerve Imaging Using Confocal Microscopy in Systemic Diseases.
studies.authors: Butt, Sameer, Rousseau, Antoine, Motulsky, Elie
studies.abstract: Corneal confocal microscopy (CCM), also referred to as in vivo confocal microscopy, is a non-invasive ophthalmic imaging technique that allows real-time visualization of the sub-basal nerve plexus and epithelial dendritic cells in the living cornea. Initially used for the diagnosis of anterior segment disorders, it has been increasingly applied to the evaluation of small-fiber involvement in systemic conditions, particularly diabetic peripheral neuropathy, in which CCM-derived parameters correlate with intraepidermal nerve fiber density (IENFD) on skin biopsy. This narrative review summarizes the technical principles of CCM, image-analysis approaches from manual tracing to deep learning, and the clinical evidence in peripheral neuropathies, central neurodegenerative diseases, autoimmune and inflammatory conditions, and long COVID. Outside diabetes, however, most data come from small, single-center, cross-sectional studies. Four barriers currently prevent CCM from becoming a routine clinical biomarker: (i) the absence of validated diagnostic thresholds and age-adjusted normative ranges outside diabetic neuropathy; (ii) the lack of disease specificity, as similar nerve loss occurs in many neurological, metabolic and ocular surface conditions; (iii) limited comparability across devices, acquisition protocols, image selection and analysis software, with automated and deep-learning tools still lacking multicenter external validation; and (iv) cost, contact-based acquisition and operator training. Overcoming these barriers will require standardized acquisition and reporting, open benchmark datasets, externally validated analysis pipelines, and large prospective longitudinal cohorts.

studies.title: The Effect of Herbal Steam Bath Therapy for Persistent Symptoms Following COVID-19: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
studies.authors: Choowong-In, Pannawat, Paithoon, Rossarin, Sriyakul, Kusuma, Kamalashiran, Chuntida et al.
studies.abstract: We evaluated whether herbal steam bath (HSB) added to standard care improved persistent symptoms following COVID-19. Sixty-eight adults were randomized equally to HSB plus standard care or standard care alone. Outcome assessors were blinded; participants and providers were unblinded. Eligibility was two weeks to six months after a negative SARS-CoV-2 test, without requiring WHO-defined post-COVID-19 condition. The HSB regimen was scheduled three times weekly for four weeks. Each session comprised three 10-min periods of herbal steam exposure, totaling 30 min of exposure. The primary outcomes were Fatigue Severity Scale (FSS) scores and seven symptom ratings at Week 4. Secondary outcomes included peak expiratory flow rate (PEFR), functional status, dyspnea grade, oxygen saturation, and vital signs. Continuous outcomes were compared using baseline-adjusted models; the seven symptom comparisons were adjusted for multiplicity using Holm's method. The adjusted between-group difference in FSS was -0.80 points (95% CI, -1.56 to -0.04; HSB plus standard care was associated with lower symptom scores and higher PEFR than standard care alone, while the FSS finding remained inconclusive. These preliminary findings support further investigation of the complete HSB intervention.

studies.title: Structural ICD-10 coding gaps and economic burden of underrecognized chronic conditions: a machine learning analysis of MEPS 2019-2022 and CDC PLACES.
studies.authors: Cece, Sinem, Pınar, Abuzer, Fuentes-Fernández, Rubén
studies.abstract: To quantify the economic burden of chronic and invisible illness using federal open data, document structural ICD-10 coding gaps, and evaluate machine learning (ML) performance for individual-level healthcare expenditure prediction. We analyzed four consecutive MEPS waves (2019-2022; Adults with ≥1 chronic condition incurred 3.3 times higher mean annual expenditures and 80% more work-loss days. Autoimmune patients faced the highest costs ($24,148-$26,630/year): 3.0-3.7× higher than adults without that specific condition, and 5.8-7.6× higher than adults with no chronic condition at all. Because the MEPS public-use file reports ICD-10-CM diagnoses only as 3-character categories, we re-ran the search at that granularity: Lyme disease remained at zero records across all four years, and long COVID in every year its code existed, but the categories containing fibromyalgia and ME-CFS were not uniformly zero and cannot be attributed to these two conditions specifically. XGBoost achieved R Lyme disease and long COVID show a genuine structural coding gap in MEPS; fibromyalgia and ME-CFS could not be confirmed present or absent, because the file merges their codes with unrelated diagnoses. ML improves expenditure prediction but cannot compensate for upstream data gaps. High disease burden co-occurring with low insurance coverage in Southern states demands targeted policy responses. Federal open data fail to capture Lyme disease and long COVID; their coding granularity cannot resolve fibromyalgia or ME-CFS from broader categories. Reforms in ICD coding, survey design, and data linkage are needed to make these populations visible to health policy and service planning.

studies.title: Resistance exercise in a chronic fatigue phenotype of Long COVID: a secondary analysis of the CISCO-21 trial.
studies.authors: Kamdar, Anna, McKinley, Gemma, Bayes, Hannah, Anderson, David et al.
studies.abstract: Among individuals with Long COVID, fatigue is a prevalent symptom. This post-hoc, secondary analysis of the multicentre randomised controlled CISCO-21 trial (NCT04900961) examined the characteristics of participants with a DePaul Symptom Questionnaire (DSQ)-defined ME/CFS-like phenotype and responses to a 3-month tailored resistance exercise programme versus usual care. The primary outcome was change in incremental shuttle walk test (ISWT) distance. Of 106 participants completing the DSQ, 45 (42.5%) had a DSQ-defined ME/CFS-like phenotype. They were younger than those without the phenotype (49.49 (9.7) vs. 54.90 (11.8) years; SMD -0.50 (-0.89, -0.10)), had similar BMI (30.41 (6.80) vs. 30.46 (5.56); SMD -0.01 (-0.39, 0.38)) and sex distribution (62.2% vs. 57.4% female), higher illness perception scores (55.07 (10.64) vs. 48.10 (12.35); SMD 0.60 (0.20, 0.99)), and lower estimated VO₂max (20.13 (6.26) vs. 22.56 (6.52) ml/kg/min; SMD -0.38 (-0.77, 0.02)).In the standard-care arm, participants without the phenotype increased by 10 m (-15, 90), versus 25 m (0, 47.5) in those with the phenotype. In the intervention arm, ISWT distance increased by 35 m (0, 120) and 35 m (10, 100), respectively. A patient-led resistance exercise programme may be feasible individuals with a DSQ-defined ME/CFS-like phenotype.

studies.title: Cardiovascular implications of COVID-19.
studies.authors: Shaib, John, Al Nakouzi, Malek, Sfeir, Lauren Christy, Arabi, Mariam
studies.abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, is now recognized as a multisystem disease with substantial cardiovascular involvement contributing to both acute and long-term morbidity. Cardiovascular manifestations range from myocardial injury and arrhythmias to thromboembolic disease, acute coronary syndromes, and heart failure, affecting both adult and pediatric populations. This narrative review provides a clinically oriented synthesis of the major cardiovascular manifestations associated with COVID-19. Current evidence indicates that myocardial injury, myocarditis, heart failure, arrhythmias, thromboembolic events, ischemic stroke, acute coronary syndromes, and pericardial disease arise through interconnected mechanisms involving endothelial dysfunction, systemic inflammation, immune dysregulation, and hypercoagulability. Older age, male sex, and pre-existing cardiovascular disease are consistently associated with worse outcomes. Although children generally experience milder disease, cardiovascular complications may occur, particularly in the setting of multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children. Emerging evidence also suggests persistent cardiovascular sequelae following acute infection, underscoring the importance of long-term surveillance and multidisciplinary follow-up, particularly among high-risk individuals. COVID-19 should be regarded as a multisystem disease with important short- and long-term cardiovascular implications. Recognizing shared pathophysiologic mechanisms may facilitate early risk stratification, targeted diagnostic evaluation, and appropriate longitudinal follow-up, particularly among high-risk populations. Further studies are needed to clarify long-term cardiovascular outcomes and optimize preventive and therapeutic strategies.

studies.title: The invisible insult: replication-independent neurotoxicity of viral and bacterial factors in post-infectious neurological syndromes.
studies.authors: Käufer, Christopher, Peelaerts, Wouter, Lau, Kristina, Kotzur, Rebecca et al.
studies.abstract: Post-viral neurological syndromes, including Neuro-PASC (long COVID), HIV-associated neurocognitive disorders, and flavivirus-associated encephalopathies, present a paradox: neurological dysfunction persists despite minimal or absent viral replication in the central nervous system (CNS), challenging the replication-dependent models of neuropathogenesis. This review synthesizes evidence for a "protein-as-pathogen" framework in which viral proteins, independent of intact virus or active replication, act as neurotoxic effectors: they breach the blood-brain barrier, activate neuroinflammatory cascades, induce neuronal death, and seed chronic proteinopathies. The same principle extends to bacterial factors such as lipopolysaccharide and curli, which converge on these pathways and point to a CNS vulnerability independent of pathogen class. We treat this as a complement to replication- and reservoir-based pathogenesis, not a replacement. We performed a comprehensive analysis of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein (S1) as a paradigmatic case study, then extended this framework through comparative analysis of human immunodeficiency virus-1 (HIV-1) gp120, flavivirus proteins (NS1, capsid, NS2A), and influenza A proteins (M1, NS1, nucleoprotein). Despite distinct viral origins and structural properties, these proteins exploit conserved host vulnerabilities. Toll-like receptor (TLR) 4 emerges as a convergent hub for microglial activation, with downstream NOD-like receptor protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome assembly amplifying neuroinflammation through interleukin (IL)-1β release. Mitochondrial dysfunction, characterized by membrane depolarization, reactive oxygen species production, and impaired mitophagy, links acute protein exposure to chronic oxidative stress and proteinopathic seeding. Neuronal death pathways show virus-specific divergence: S1 induces necroptosis via NRP1/RIPK1, gp120 triggers apoptosis through CXCR4/CCR5 acting in concert with microglia-derived neurotoxins, and ZIKV envelope protein activates PARP-1-dependent parthanatos. All proteins converge on IL-1β-mediated inflammatory neuronal killing and complement-dependent synaptic elimination that persists beyond detectable viral clearance. The protein-as-pathogen framework reveals mechanistic unity across superficially disparate post-viral and post-bacterial syndromes and identifies druggable convergent pathways, including TLR4, NLRP3, complement, and mitochondrial targets, amenable to therapeutic intervention with existing compounds. This framework has direct implications for diagnosis (protein biomarkers), prognosis (determinants of protein persistence), and treatment (protein-targeted versus downstream anti-inflammatory strategies) of post-viral neurological disease.

studies.title: Sleep and mental health outcomes following SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy: A matched cross-sectional study.
studies.authors: Booker, Lauren A, Howard, Mark E, Czeisler, Mark É, Facer-Childs, Elise R et al.
studies.abstract: This study aimed to compare sleep quality, mental health symptoms, and PASC outcomes among pregnant and non-pregnant participants with and without prior COVID-19 infection. A matched cross-sectional study design was undertaken, comparing four groups: 1) Not Pregnant, no prior COVID-19; 2) Not Pregnant, prior COVID-19; 3) Pregnant, no prior COVID-19; and 4) Pregnant and prior COVID-19. A total of 1,868 women were included in the analysis (934 pregnant and 934 not pregnant). Among participants with prior COVID-19, those who were pregnant had significantly more comorbidities, and higher hospitalization rates, compared to those not pregnant with prior COVID-19. Overall, prior COVID-19 infection was consistently associated with poorer sleep quality and more sleep disturbances, regardless of pregnancy status. In addition, participants who were pregnant with prior COVID-19 were more likely to report a shorter sleep duration of <5 and <6 hours per night, compared with those not pregnant with no prior COVID-19. Adjusted analyses showed pregnant participants with prior COVID-19 had worse sleep quality and more frequent sleep problems than non-pregnant participants without prior COVID-19. Furthermore, those who were pregnant with prior COVID-19 had a 1.76 to 2.69 times increased odds of developing PASC symptoms, compared to those not pregnant. These high rates of persistent PASC symptoms reported at 3 and 6 months, indicating more prolonged or delayed symptom expression. They also experienced worse mental health outcomes, with the prevalence ratio of having depression and anxiety symptoms occurring 1.89 and 1.72 times higher, respectively, among pregnant individuals with a history of COVID-19. Prior COVID-19 infection should be considered when assessing sleep and mental health in pregnancy due to its association with long-term PASC symptoms. Tailored post-COVID care, maternal health policies, and vaccination should be prioritized.

studies.title: The Lung-Brain-Immune Axis: Mechanistic Pathways Linking Pulmonary Inflammation to Neuropsychiatric and Neurological Disease.
studies.authors: Rawson, Clayton, Mittal, Agastya, Al-Nuaimy, Yusor, Hwang, Isaac et al.
studies.abstract: Chronic respiratory diseases and neuropsychiatric and neurological disorders contribute substantially to the global disease burden but have traditionally been studied as distinct organ-system disorders. Emerging evidence supports an integrated lung-brain-immune axis through which pulmonary inflammation can alter central nervous system (CNS) function and contribute to neurological and neuropsychiatric disease. This review synthesizes preclinical and clinical literature examining the anatomical, immunological, environmental, and clinical mechanisms linking pulmonary inflammation to CNS dysfunction. Evidence was synthesized across neural and immune communication pathways, inflammatory signaling, environmental and infectious triggers, disease-specific associations, lifespan susceptibility, and translational applications. Lung-brain communication is bidirectional and occurs through vagal and autonomic neural pathways, circulating inflammatory mediators including interleukin (IL)-1β, IL-6, and tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, immune-cell trafficking, and disruption of the alveolar-capillary and blood-brain barriers. These processes promote microglial priming, astrocyte reactivity, oxidative stress, and synaptic dysfunction, providing a cellular basis for cognitive and affective symptoms. Air pollution, respiratory viruses, allergens, and tobacco smoke can activate these pathways, which are implicated in asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, acute respiratory distress syndrome, long COVID, and interstitial lung disease. Susceptibility varies across the lifespan, from prenatal immune activation and adolescence to immunosenescence. Emerging biomarkers, anti-inflammatory and neuromodulatory therapies, and immune-phenotype-based stratification may enable more targeted interventions. The lung-brain-immune axis provides a unifying biological framework in which pulmonary inflammation can act as a modifiable driver of neuroimmune dysfunction. Mechanistically validated causal models and longitudinal human studies are needed to clarify disease-specific pathways and translate these insights into clinical practice.

studies.title: Unraveling the Nexus: Long-Term Impact of COVID-19 on Alzheimer's Disease Progression in the Aging Population: An Observational Cross-Sectional Study with a Short-Term Longitudinal Follow-up Component.
studies.authors: Abiri, Elaheh, Raesi, Rasoul
studies.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic strained healthcare systems worldwide, particularly in caring for individuals with pre-existing health conditions. This study aims to examine the long-term association between COVID-19 and Alzheimer's in elderly patients following the acute phase of the pandemic. This observational cross-sectional study with short-term follow-up was conducted in 2024 among 200 older adults (≥65 years) recruited from neurology clinics in Damghan, Iran. Participants were divided into four groups (50 per group): healthy controls, AD patients without COVID-19, AD patients with mild COVID-19, and AD patients with severe COVID-19. Cognitive function was assessed using MMSE, and genomic instability was measured through the Comet assay. Group comparisons, correlation analysis, and multivariable regression were performed, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. Our results indicate that individuals who are both infected with COVID-19 and have Alzheimer's had a higher level of DNA damage and instability than individuals without the two conditions. A notable increase in DNA breakage was observed among individuals who had experienced a severe case of COVID-19 in the past, which may be connected to accelerated brain deterioration. In addition, the cognitive decline in patients with more genomic instability was more pronounced and might be an indication of worsening Alzheimer's after COVID-19. The observation that DNA damage is associated with cognitive decline provides us with novel concepts on how we can treat patients who are recovering from COVID-19. This paper highlights the need to understand the effects of COVID-19 on brain health, particularly in older adults with Alzheimer's disease. Our findings suggest that genomic stability may serve as a key indicator for measuring long-term brain outcomes, potentially informing new approaches to addressing cognitive issues after COVID-19.

studies.title: Identification of altered potassium channels for drug repurposing in long COVID patients.
studies.authors: George, John P, Gaikwad, Kiran Bharat, Sharma, Jyoti
studies.abstract: Long COVID (LC) is a complex condition characterized by persistent, chronic multisystem manifestations, with a significant proportion of patients exhibiting neurological symptoms. Human ion channels (HICs), particularly potassium channels, are abundantly expressed in the nervous system and are involved in key physiological processes, making them potential candidates for understanding LC pathophysiology and identifying opportunities for drug repurposing. Meta-analysis of RNA sequencing datasets from COVID-19-recovered and LC patients was performed. Differential gene expression analysis, functional enrichment analysis, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis were performed to uncover key genes, pathways, and co-expression modules consisting of HICs, lipid metabolism-, and immune signaling-related genes. Drug-gene interaction analysis was performed using the Drug-Gene Interaction Database and Connectivity Map to identify potential ion channel candidates for drug repurposing. A total of 715 dysregulated genes, including 18 HICs, were identified, among which seven were potassium channels. Three significant modules containing HICs, lipid metabolism-, and immune signaling-related genes were identified and found to be associated with antigen processing and presentation, complement and coagulation cascades, and cytokine-related pathways. Additionally, drug interaction analysis identified approved drugs targeting These findings provide insights into a subset of molecular alterations underlying the multisystem dysregulation observed in LC. The identified drug interactions may provide opportunities for drug repurposing to address neurological manifestations of LC. Further experimental validation is required to establish their therapeutic efficacy and potential clinical relevance.

studies.title: Long COVID, chronic fatigue syndrome, and chronic lyme disease as Post-acute Infection Syndromes (PAIS): a translational synthesis.
studies.authors: Sewell, Patrick E, Reddy, Rohan
studies.abstract: Post-acute infection syndromes (PAIS) comprise a heterogeneous group of chronic, multisystem conditions characterized by persistent or relapsing symptoms following resolution of an acute infectious illness, in the absence of ongoing pathogen replication detectable by standard diagnostics. Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS), Long COVID, post-treatment Lyme disease syndrome, and related entities are increasingly recognized as part of a shared post-infectious disease spectrum. The COVID-19 pandemic has markedly expanded the global burden of PAIS and intensified investigation into their biological underpinnings. This narrative translational review integrates clinical, epidemiologic, genetic, immunologic, metabolic, and neurovascular evidence to propose a unified framework for PAIS pathophysiology and management. We anchor the review in clinical phenomenology before turning to mechanism, then provide depth treatment of three core mechanism areas-cellular immune dysfunction with T-cell exhaustion and immunometabolic reprogramming, viral and antigen persistence with herpesvirus reactivation, and the genetic architecture revealed by the DecodeME 2025 GWAS and complementary studies. Convergent mechanisms across PAIS include T-cell exhaustion phenotypes, NK cell cytotoxicity defects, immunometabolic reprogramming with mitochondrial bioenergetic inefficiency, autonomic and endothelial dysfunction, neuroinflammation, altered tryptophan-kynurenine-NAD PAIS represent biologically grounded, systems-level disorders with shared mechanisms and heterogeneous clinical expression. Integrating molecular insights with pragmatic clinical frameworks may accelerate development of precision-oriented diagnostic and therapeutic strategies to address the growing global impact of post-infectious chronic illness.

studies.title: Stigma concerns and depressive symptoms among people ever infected with COVID-19 in Hong Kong: cross-sectional mediation via perceived stress and maladaptive cognitive emotion regulation.
studies.authors: Yu, Yanqiu, Lau, Mason M C, Lau, Joseph T F
studies.abstract: Stigma concerns are common during outbreaks of emerging respiratory infectious diseases and have been associated with mental distress such as depressive symptoms. This study investigated the associations between stigma concerns related to COVID-19 infection and depressive symptoms among people who had ever contracted COVID-19 (PECC), and whether these associations would be significantly mediated by perceived stress and maladaptive cognitive emotion regulation of rumination and catastrophizing. A population-based, random, and anonymous cross-sectional telephone survey was conducted among Chinese adults (aged ≥ 18 years) in Hong Kong who self-reported having ever tested positive for COVID-19 (n = 277) from June to August 2022, during the territory's fifth-wave outbreak. Structural equation modeling (SEM) were used to test the indirect associations, adjusting for background factors (employment status, chronic disease status, knowing people having long COVID, and history of home quarantine due to own COVID-19 infection). The prevalence of mild or more severe depressive symptoms was 8%, and overall symptom levels were low. Adjusting for background factors, stigma concerns, perceived stress, rumination, and catastrophizing were positively associated with depressive symptoms. The SEM result showed that the association between stigma concerns and depressive symptoms was significantly mediated by indirect paths via perceived stress alone and via perceived stress followed by maladaptive cognitive emotion regulation; the direct association between stigma concerns and depressive symptoms was statistically non-significant. Among PECC with generally low depressive symptom levels, stigma concerns were positively associated with depressive symptoms, and this association was significantly mediated via elevated perceived stress and maladaptive cognitive emotion regulation. If corroborated, interventions addressing stigma concerns, stress management, and emotional regulation skills may benefit this population, and stigma-related distress warrants early monitoring in future outbreaks of respiratory infectious diseases.

studies.title: Multi-model forecasting of respiratory disease activity in Germany during the 2024-2025 season.
studies.authors: Bracher, Johannes, Wolffram, Daniel, Amaral Lind, Rodrigo, Bardeck, Nils et al.
studies.abstract: Respiratory diseases cause considerable morbidity in autumn and winter and are a priority in public health monitoring. In Germany, they are subject to a number of surveillance systems, including both pathogen-specific and syndromic indicators. In this paper we present a collaborative multi-target and multi-model real-time forecasting system rolled out during the 2024/25 season, and discuss differences to earlier efforts carried out during the COVID-19 pandemic. We focus on general practitioner consultations for acute respiratory infections (ARI) and hospitalizations for severe acute respiratory infections (SARI), where a total of eight models were run to generate nowcasts and forecasts. In addition, we consider confirmed cases of seasonal influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) where one forecasting model each was available. As all indicators were subject to retrospective revisions, forecasting models were combined with a nowcasting step. For the SARI and ARI indicators, we combined the available models into an ensemble and conducted detailed quantitative evaluations. Nowcasts overall showed convincing performance, even though for some models Christmas break effects led to an upward bias in early January. Forecasts were overall well-calibrated and most models outperformed simple benchmark models. When taking into account age-stratified targets, most observed performance differences to a persistence baseline were statistically significant. Anticipating the peak timing and magnitude, however, proved to be challenging, with many models predicting too flat curves with a too early turnaround (e.g., in late January rather than mid-February for SARI). The combined ensemble forecast was among the best-performing approaches, but unlike in previous related projects did not consistently outperform individual models. We conclude by discussing learnings on the organization of collaborative forecasting projects in post-COVID-19 times.

studies.title: Hepatic EPHX1 potentiates liver fibrosis by decreasing eicosatrienoic acids.
studies.authors: Ikenaga, Hiroko, Matsubara, Tsutomu, Enomoto, Masaru, Sato-Matsubara, Misako et al.
studies.abstract: Changes in polyunsaturated fatty acid metabolites are thought to contribute to pathogeneses of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and liver fibrosis. This study demonstrated that hepatic microsomal epoxide hydrolase (EPHX1) promotes liver fibrosis by decreasing hepatic eicosatrienoic acid (EET) levels, suggesting that elevation of serum dihydroxyeicosatrienoic acid (DHET) levels is an indicator of advanced fibrosis. Serum lipidomic analysis of 102 patients with MASLD and 121 with chronic hepatitis C, combined with multivariate logistic regression, confirmed elevation of serum 11,12-DHET levels as a predictor of advanced fibrosis. The expression of hepatic EPHX1, which hydrolyzes EET to DHET, increased in patients with advanced fibrosis. MASLD mouse model showed increased hepatic EPHX1 levels and decreased hepatic EET levels. Ephx1-null mice showed suppressed hepatic fibrogenesis and oxidative stress with increasing EET levels. In hepatic stellate cells (HSCs), treatment with 11,12-EET reduced COL1A1 expression, but not 11,12-DHET, attenuated intracellular oxidative stress, and suppressed TGF-β-induced HSC activation. Furthermore, it alleviated liver fibrosis by attenuating hepatic oxidative stress and suppressing HSC activation in mice with thioacetamide-induced liver fibrosis. This study provides evidence that EPHX1 contributes to EET hydrolysis in the liver and participates in liver fibrogenesis, suggesting its potential as a therapeutic target.

studies.title: Targeting KCa3.1 channels in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma impairs disease progression.
studies.authors: Soret, Benjamin, Neumann, Ilka, Wilczak, Weronika, Rugi, Micol et al.
studies.abstract: This study explores the therapeutic potential of the calcium-activated potassium channel KCa3.1 in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Increased KCa3.1 expression correlates with poor overall survival of patients with PDAC. Using the immunocompetent KPfC (KrasWT/LSL-G12D Tp53fl/+ Pdx1-Cre) mouse model, we evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of KCa3.1 inhibition with TRAM-34 and maurotoxin alone or in combination with gemcitabine. Mechanistic insights were obtained in vitro from KCa3.1 CRISPR knockout pancreatic cancer cells (PANC-1KCNN4-/-) and a three-dimensional mixed spheroid model composed of pancreatic cancer and stellate cells. In vivo, KCa3.1 inhibition combined with gemcitabine decreased growth of tumor nodes and counteracted gemcitabine-induced fibrosis. Consistently, in vitro and ex vivo data showed that KCa3.1 inhibition induced tumor cell death and altered the invasive phenotype. Here, maurotoxin outperformed TRAM-34. On a molecular level, KCa3.1 inhibition diminished epithelial-mesenchymal transition, reduced T cell exhaustion markers and TGF-β1 secretion, and downregulated the G2-M checkpoint. These findings can mechanistically account for the therapeutic benefits of targeting KCa3.1 channels in PDAC.

studies.title: Association Between Myocardial BOLD Reactivity and Peripheral Microvascular Function Assessed by Flow-Mediated Skin Fluorescence.
studies.authors: Castelein, Johannes, Sabisz, Agnieszka, Glińska, Anna, Żarczyńska-Buchowiecka, Marta et al.
studies.abstract: Cardiac blood oxygen level-dependent (BOLD) MRI during breath-hold provides a contrast-free myocardial-specific readout of vasoreactivity. We tested whether myocardial BOLD reactivity covaries with peripheral microvascular function measured by flow-mediated skin fluorescence (FMSF), thereby assessing concordance between two physiologically distinct vascular beds. Twenty-eight participants underwent a mid-diastolic cardiac BOLD MRI at 1.5 T during end-expiratory breath-hold, alongside forearm FMSF during transient brachial artery occlusion. Participants were classified as having FMSF-normal reactivity (NR) or FMSF-abnormal reactivity (AR) based on predefined FMSF criteria (i.e., one or more of the following: reactive hyperemia response [RHR] < 30% or hypoxia sensitivity [HS] < 25). studies.title: Comprehensive review of myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome.
studies.authors: Jeyaraman, Madhan, Jeyaraman, Naveen, Ramasubramanian, Swaminathan, Schäfer, Luise et al.
studies.abstract: Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) is a complex, debilitating disease that is unexplained and is characterised by persistent unexplained fatigue, Post Exertional Malaise (PEM), cognitive impairment, unrefreshing sleep and multisystem impairment. Despite the high burden of symptoms and the worldwide prevalence, ME/CFS has been poorly understood, underdiagnosed and underfunded. This large-scale review summarises the available evidence regarding the epidemiology, diagnostic progress, main clinical characteristics, pathophysiological theories and therapeutic approaches for ME/CFS. Despite problems with diagnostic consistency, the lack of validated biomarkers, and historical linkage to psychiatric illness, the recognition of this condition has been delayed and has led to patient marginalisation. The review highlights PEM as a cardinal symptom and reviews the weaknesses in earlier diagnostic criteria, as well as current changes in treatment guidelines, including the formal withdrawal of Graded Exercise Therapy, which has evidence of harm. New pathophysiological evidence suggests mitochondrial dysfunction, immune dysregulation, autonomic imbalance, neuroinflammation, and alterations in gut microbiome. New diagnostic and therapeutic strategies, such as metabolomic and electrophysiological assays, mTOR inhibitors, and decentralised clinical trial designs, are being studied. This intersection with Long COVID offers a chance to rapidly advance studies of post-infectious chronic diseases. The paper also argues for stringent subtyping, uniform data collection, and ongoing patient participation in research as strategies to surmount challenges of heterogeneity. Finally, it underscores the critical need for fair funding of research, so biomarker discovery and development of disease-modifying treatments can be achieved. The care of people with ME/CFS is not only a clinical obligation, but also a public health one.

studies.title: Balancing Trained Immunity and Tolerance: Innate Immunity Crossroads in COVID-19 Vaccination.
studies.authors: Lima-Silva, Lincon Felipe, Angelim, Monara Kaélle Sérvulo Cruz, Moraes-Vieira, Pedro M
studies.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has underscored the critical role of immune responses in determining disease severity, with SARS-CoV-2 infection triggering both protective and pathological reactions. While adaptive immunity (mediated by neutralizing antibodies and memory T cells) has been the primary focus of vaccination strategies, emerging evidence highlights the importance of innate immune adaptation, a spectrum of states ranging from trained immunity, in which innate immune cells undergo epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming, enhancing rapid, broad-spectrum antiviral defenses, to innate immune tolerance, in which persistent stimulation renders the same cells hyporesponsive. In this review, we frame SARS-CoV-2 infection and COVID-19 vaccination as opposing forces along this training-tolerance continuum, and we distinguish three levels of evidence: persistent epigenetic and metabolic marks, altered responses to a secondary challenge, and demonstrable effects on clinical outcomes. We discuss how pattern recognition receptors initiate antiviral responses, how metabolic reprogramming influences immune cell behavior, and how trained immunity extends beyond leukocytes to airway epithelial and endothelial cells. Trained immunity inducers, such as Bacillus Calmette-Guérin vaccination, show promise in preclinical studies but yield mixed clinical results, highlighting the challenges of translating innate immune modulation into therapeutic benefits. We further examine how SARS-CoV-2 itself can act as a natural inducer of trained immunity, how maladaptive resolution of this program may contribute to long COVID, and why only a subset of infected individuals develops post-acute sequelae. Finally, we consider the post-pandemic immunological landscape, including immune debt and the resurgence of unrelated infections due to reduced microbial exposure, and the lessons these hold for vaccines against future emerging respiratory viruses. Future vaccination strategies should aim to promote context-appropriate innate antiviral responses while limiting maladaptive inflammatory persistence, integrating innate immune regulation with durable adaptive protection against SARS-CoV-2 and emerging respiratory pathogens.

studies.title: Disentangling Confounders from Pathology in Long-COVID Trajectory Prediction for Women: An Interpretable Large-Language-Model Approach.
studies.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
studies.authors: Wang, Jing, Galis, Zorina, Zhang, Tong, Luo, Yiming et al.
studies.abstract: Post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC, "Long COVID") disproportionately affects women, in whom hallmark symptoms-insomnia, fatigue, palpitations, cognitive difficulty-overlap with comorbidities and hormonal transitions such as menopause. This diagnostic overlap is a confounding problem: models that forecast future symptom severity risk attributing baseline physiological noise to viral pathology. We ask whether an interpretable, causally disentangled language model can separate true pathological signal from such confounders while remaining competitive with strong predictors of future PASC severity. Retrospective cohort of 1,155 adult women (median age 61) from the NIH RECOVER program, combining static clinical profiles, longitudinal symptom surveys, and four weeks of mean-aggregated consumer-wearable physiology (heart rate, sleep, activity). We render each patient as a natural-language clinical narrative and fine-tune a small open-weight language model (Qwen2.5-0.5B, LoRA) with an attention-based Long-COVID severity is strongly autocorrelated, so last-value carry-forward is a hard reference and is the most accurate method on the full cohort (MAE 3.02 For static, slowly evolving patients a simple carry-forward forecast is hard to beat and should be the reference any PASC model is judged against. The value of a learned, disentangled model is (i) better accuracy where trajectories are dynamic and (ii) an interpretable, "clinically honest" attribution that down-weights confounders such as menopause-reducing the risk of misattributing baseline physiology to Long COVID. Long COVID is more common and often more severe in women, but many of its symptoms look like other common conditions or like the normal changes of menopause. When a computer model tries to predict how a patient's symptoms will evolve, it can be fooled into blaming Long COVID for what is really background physiology. We built a model based on a small language model that reads a written summary of each patient-their history, comorbidities, and a month of wearable-device data-and is explicitly trained to separate "true disease signal" from "background noise." We tested it against standard predictors at 3, 6, and 9 months. We report an finding that is easy to overlook: because Long COVID severity changes slowly, simply assuming a patient's next score equals their last score is very accurate and hard to beat for stable patients. studies.title: Symptom-based phenotypes and health-related quality of life in Spanish patients with long COVID: a latent class analysis.
studies.authors: Domínguez-Martín, Andrea, Suárez-Moreno, Nuria, Navarro-Cáceres, Alicia, Arroyo-Romero, Silvia et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID presents with heterogeneous, fluctuating symptoms that markedly reduce health-related quality of life (HRQol). This study aimed to identify symptom-based subgroups of patients with Long COVID using Latent Class Analysis (LCA) and to compare health-related quality of life across the identified classes. A cross-sectional study was conducted in Salamanca, Spain. Adults with Long COVID per WHO criteria were recruited from primary care and a specialized post-COVID unit.
