studies.title: Short-, medium- and long-term sequelae following COVID-19 infection: a network cohort study across multiple Asia-Pacific regions.
studies.journal: The Lancet regional health. Western Pacific
studies.authors: Zhang, Ran, Lam, Ivan Chun Hang, Chai, Yi, Liu, Xinyi et al.
studies.abstract: Existing evidence on post-COVID-19 sequelae were largely derived from single-database studies among western population with limited generalizability. This multi-regional study aimed to characterize the risk of clinical sequelae across multiple organ systems over short- (0-90 days), medium- (91-365 days) and long-term (>365 days) phases following SARS-CoV-2 infection among the Asia-Pacific population. A retrospective cohort study was conducted using electronic medical records or claims data from New Zealand, Korea, Taiwan and Hong Kong. Patients with COVID-19 infection and their matched controls (non-COVID-19 infection) were included in our study. Propensity scores were estimated via logistic regression incorporating age group, sex, comorbidities and vaccination status; cases were matched 1:4 to controls within a 0.1- standard deviation caliper. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for all-cause mortality and incident clinical sequelae across three follow-up windows. A random-effects meta-analysis was employed to combine the effect estimates from separate database. This study included 346,882 individuals with COVID-19 and 1,339,095 matched non-infected comparators. In the short-term, COVID-19 was associated with markedly elevated risk of all-cause mortality [Hazard Ratio (HR): 7.57; 95% CI (6.30, 9.11)] and higher risk of interstitial lung disease [7.25 (2.24, 23.48)], acute respiratory distress syndrome [7.84 (4.45, 13.81)], heart failure [2.20 (1.18, 4.11)] and coronary artery disease [2.18 (1.55, 3.05)]. In the medium- and long-term, risks of some clinical conditions such as cardiovascular disease (Medium-term: 1.04 (0.85, 1.29); Long-term 1.07 (0.60, 1.89) subsided, but significant risk remained for certain respiratory disease such as ARDS (Medium-term:1.38 (1.05, 1.81)). Patients with aged over 65 years, or with multimorbidity (Charlson Comorbidity Index ≥4), or with a reinfection of COVID-19, have a higher risk of developing clinical sequelae than their opposing subgroup of patients. Patients from the Asia-Pacific population with COVID-19 experience a diverse short-term multi-organ complications and elevated mortality, with the risk of most sequelae diminishing over time. These findings are consistent with those observed in Western populations. Additionally, the results from this study highlight the need for focused monitoring of complications involving respiratory and cardiovascular diseases, and emphasize the ongoing importance of reinfection prevention among the Asia-Pacific population. This work was supported by Collaborative Research Fund, University Grants Committee, the HKSAR Government (Ref. No. C7154-20GF).

studies.title: Predictors and prevalence of symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing four years after COVID-19: a prospective observational study.
studies.authors: Hallberg, Carl, Svensson-Raskh, Anna, Fagevik Olsén, Monika, Svensson, Annie et al.
studies.abstract: Dysfunctional breathing is increasingly recognised among individuals with post-COVID-19 condition (PCC), yet data on long-term prevalence and predictors are scarce. This study assessed the prevalence of symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing, as indicated by elevated Nijmegen questionnaire (NQ) scores, four years after COVID-19 illness in adults with PCC and identified associated factors and baseline predictors by comparing individuals with and without elevated NQ scores. In this prospective observational study, adults with PCC, both previously hospitalised and non-hospitalised for COVID-19, were recruited from a specialised post-COVID outpatient clinic. Baseline assessments (2020-2022) were analysed together with data from a digital follow-up survey in 2024. Symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing was defined as a NQ score ≥ 23 at follow-up. Between group differences were examined, and multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify associated factors and baseline predictors. Among 288 participants (median follow-up 50 months), 143 (50%) had symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing. These individuals were younger, often female, and more frequently non-hospitalised during acute COVID-19. Baseline predictors included non-hospitalisation, higher dyspnoea severity, lower FEV1, and younger age. At four years, elevated NQ scores (≥ 23) were independently associated with higher dyspnoea severity, greater PCC-symptom burden, depressive symptoms and postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome. Individuals with symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing performed worse in the six-minute walk test, one-minute sit to stand test, and maximal inspiratory pressure test at baseline, whereas lung function did not differ. Patient-reported outcomes were consistently worse compared with those with NQ scores < 23 and improved less over time. Half of the individuals with PCC in this cohort reported symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing four years after COVID-19, as indicated by a NQ score ≥ 23. Elevated NQ scores were associated with greater PCC-symptom burden and poorer health outcomes, highlighting their potential clinical relevance in long-term PCC. Future studies should combine patient-reported measures with objective assessment of breathing pattern and ventilatory function.

studies.title: Association between quantitative computed tomography metrics and pulmonary function in patients with post-COVID-19 pulmonary fibrosis: a single-center cross-sectional study.
studies.authors: Bayaraa, Odonchimeg, Lamid-Ochir, Oyunbold, Galbadrakh, Ninjbadgar, Bayarsaikhan, Dalai et al.
studies.abstract: Post-COVID-19 pulmonary fibrosis is an important long-term complication of severe SARS-CoV-2 infection. Quantitative computed tomography (QCT) provides observer-independent measurement of parenchymal abnormality. However, the association between structural lung abnormalities and functional impairment remains insufficiently characterized. We quantified the cross-sectional association between a CT-derived density metric and pulmonary function, exercise capacity and dyspnea. Single-center cross-sectional study of 39 adults assessed approximately one year after severe COVID-19 pneumonia; each underwent one chest CT and one pulmonary function assessment, with no serial imaging or serial physiology. QCT was performed in 3D Slicer v5.0.3 with the Lung CT Analyzer extension. Collapse percentage (collapse%) was defined as the volume of intrapulmonary tissue with attenuation above - 400 HU, after exclusion of vessels (> 0 HU), divided by total lung volume (TLV) - the non-aerated compartment of the established CT aeration model. Spirometry followed the 2019 ATS/ERS standards; exercise capacity was assessed by 6-minute walk distance (6MWD) with Borg dyspnea scoring. Correlation coefficients are reported with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO) was unavailable. Mean age was 56.7 ± 11.4 years and 19 of 39 participants (48.7%) were male. Mean TLV was 4070.2 ± 1529.5 mL and mean collapse% was 5.4 ± 5.2%. Collapse% was inversely associated with 6MWD (r = - 0.59, 95% CI - 0.76 to - 0.34; p < 0.0001), with FVC % predicted (r = - 0.46, - 0.68 to - 0.17; p < 0.001) and, to a lesser extent, with FEV1% predicted (r = - 0.32, - 0.58 to - 0.00; p < 0.05), corresponding to 35%, 21% and 10% of shared variance. Collapse% was higher in participants with a Borg score of 2-4 than in those scoring 0-1 (p = 0.03). Quantitative CT provided a structural measure of residual lung involvement, while pulmonary function tests measured the associated physiological impairment; the two were only weakly to moderately associated, indicating that they are complementary rather than interchangeable. As a cross-sectional, single-center study of severe-disease survivors without gas transfer measurement or serial imaging, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require longitudinal validation before quantitative CT can be used to inform diagnosis, monitoring, or management.

studies.title: Global Prevalence and Correlates of Stigma in Long COVID: A Systematic Scoping Review of Quantitative Evidence.
studies.journal: Journal of epidemiology and global health
studies.authors: Becerra-García, Juan Antonio, Martínez-Suárez, Pedro Carlos, Barbeito, Sara
studies.abstract: Long COVID is a multisystem syndrome with a high global prevalence that impacts the physical and psychosocial well-being of affected individuals. While its clinical manifestations are well-documented, the illness-related stigma as an emerging topic remains poorly characterized from a quantitative perspective. This scoping review aimed to map the global quantitative evidence regarding the prevalence, manifestation, psychometric assessment, and factors associated with stigma in individuals with Long COVID. A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, PsycINFO, and Web of Science following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines and the Arksey and O'Malley framework. Quantitative empirical studies examining stigma in Long COVID populations worldwide were included. Methodological quality was evaluated using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Out of 809 identified documents, eight articles published between 2022 and 2026 that met the selection criteria were included, representing 2925 participants. The findings revealed a high prevalence of stigma (75.9% to 83%), manifesting mainly in anticipated and internalized forms (64.2% to 90.8%). Three primary measurement tools were identified, with the Long-COVID Stigma Scale emerging as the most widely validated and used instrument. Higher levels of stigma were significantly associated with poorer mental health, lower quality of life, and reduced well-being. The psychologization of symptoms was associated with increased stigma, while self-related processes (such as self-coldness and reduced self-compassion) appeared to mediate its negative impact on well-being. Furthermore, a preliminary stigma vulnerability profile was identified, highlighting women, younger individuals, and those with a formal Long COVID clinical diagnosis as experiencing higher stigma levels. Stigma appears to be a central component of the illness experience in Long COVID, carrying important public health and psychosocial implications. Our findings underscore the need for coordinated and multisectoral public health research efforts to address this stigma and improve patient well-being. This research agenda should include studies evaluating population-level socio-educational campaigns to raise awareness about Long COVID stigma, the integration of stigma-informed training into clinical protocols, and the potential value of incorporating validated psychometric screening instruments into routine practice to evaluate their impact on vulnerable patient populations.

studies.title: Timing dependent associations of acute phase laboratory and antibody parameters with post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection in unvaccinated individuals.
studies.authors: Yamamoto, Shinya, Ohtsuka, Takeshi, Kishi, Yoshiro, Okamoto, Koh et al.
studies.abstract: Post-acute sequelae of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection (PASC) affects a substantial minority of individuals after acute COVID-19, and immune dysregulation is widely implicated in its pathogenesis. Reported associations between SARS-CoV-2-specific antibody responses and PASC have nonetheless been inconsistent. Because antibody levels change rapidly in the weeks after symptom onset, the timing of sampling may itself account for much of this heterogeneity, yet few studies have examined humoral responses along the time axis from symptom onset in combination with routinely available hematological, biochemical, and coagulation parameters. Eight hundred seventy-two serial serum samples were retrospectively analyzed from 213 unvaccinated individuals experiencing their first SARS-CoV-2 infection, sampled between April 2020 and June 2021, before vaccine rollout and before the emergence of Omicron; 13 individuals subsequently met the World Health Organization definition of PASC. Sixty-seven parameters, comprising antiviral antibodies, autoantibodies and immune markers, complete blood count, biochemistry and coagulation tests, were compared between groups within four windows defined by days since symptom onset: ≤ 7, 8-14, 15-28, and > 28 days. The pattern of association shifted markedly across windows. Within seven days of onset, innate inflammatory and coagulation markers predominated. Between days 8 and 14, when adaptive humoral responses first become measurable, red cell indices differed between groups, with lower mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration remaining significant when each patient contributed a single value. Anti-spike IgM levels tended to be higher in individuals who later developed PASC, although the difference was not statistically significant. Exploratory multivariable models combining humoral and hematological features discriminated better than either domain alone, although the small number of PASC cases precludes any claim of predictive validity. These findings identify days 8-14 after symptom onset as a potentially informative window during which acute-phase laboratory parameters, and possibly early humoral responses, differ between individuals who do and do not subsequently develop PASC, and suggest that the timing and quality of the early antibody response, rather than antibody magnitude measured at a single late time point, merit systematic investigation in PASC.

studies.title: Extracellular galectin-3 preferentially through CD44 and PD-1 binds activated T cells and marks memory-phenotype T cell subsets.
studies.authors: Abouda, Amal, Alimo, Emmanuel T, Azimi, Ako, Bigleri, AmirAli et al.
studies.abstract: Galectin-3 (Gal-3) is a multifunctional β-galactoside-binding lectin implicated in immune regulation, yet its association with T cell phenotypes under physiological and inflammatory conditions remains incompletely defined. We investigated Gal-3 expression and binding on murine and human T cells across developmental stages, tissues, sex, genetic background, circadian time, and inflammatory disease settings. In mice, Gal-3-associated CD4 Our findings identify Gal-3 as a context-dependent marker and potential regulator of activated, antigen-experienced T cells, which promotes T cell apoptosis.

studies.title: Comparative analysis of SNPs associated with COVID-19 and chronic liver disease identifies DPP9 as a candidate genetic marker for Long COVID.
studies.authors: da Silva, Lucas Lima, Maya-Miles, Douglas, Maul, Juliana Cardoso, Paulo, Iolanda Raquel Ferreira et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID is a multisystemic condition characterized by persistent symptoms after acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, whose biological mechanisms are not yet fully understood. Host genetic factors may be associated, and the sharing of genetic architecture with other chronic diseases such as viral hepatitis B and C may aid in understanding this disease. A cross-sectional study was conducted including 150 individuals stratified into two groups: (i) Long COVID and (ii) chronic viral hepatitis B and C. Eighteen single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) previously associated with COVID-19 severity and inflammatory pathways were genotyped using TaqMan® real-time PCR assays. The analyses of genetic association models were performed using multivariate logistic regression adjusted for gender, self-reported skin color, and comorbidities. Mental health scales for assessing depression (Beck), anxiety (Hamilton), fatigue, and post-COVID functional scale were used both to define the syndrome and for subsequent analyses of the genotypic profile probably associated with Long COVID. Among all the SNPs analyzed, rs12610495 (A/G) in the DPP9 gene was the only variant consistently associated with Long COVID. After adjustment for sex, self-reported skin color, and hepatitis status, carriers of the G variant allele demonstrated increased odds of Long COVID under the dominant model (OR = 2.66; 95% CI: 1.08-6.57; p = 0.029) and the overdominant model (OR = 2.96; 95% CI: 1.17-7.52; p = 0.018). The association was more pronounced in women (OR = 3.30; 95% CI: 1.08-10.07). Exploratory analyses of mental and functional outcomes did not reach statistical significance, although a higher frequency of functional limitation and fatigue was observed among carriers of the G allele. This study suggests that DPP9 rs12610495 is associated with Long COVID, previously associated only with severe acute COVID, demonstrating that individuals carrying the rs12610495 G variant allele had higher odds of developing Long COVID. The inclusion of viral hepatitis as a chronic inflammatory condition for comparison contributed to the identification of shared genetic archetypal among diseases, revealing the possible role of DPP9 with Long COVID and highlighting this gene as a relevant target for future validation studies.

studies.title: Real-world effectiveness of early nirmatrelvir/ritonavir initiation after COVID-19 diagnosis in outpatient setting against severe illness, hospitalization, death, and long COVID in N3C.
studies.authors: Makkar, Steve R, Hansen, Kristen, Yadaw, Arjun S, Tripler, Therese et al.
studies.abstract: COVID-19 has placed a monumental burden on the health care system globally. Although no longer a public health emergency, there is still a pressing need for effective treatments that prevent adverse outcomes associated with this disease. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir (NMV-R) is a promising and potentially effective antiviral, which until recently was under emergency use authorization. Our objective was to evaluate the real-world effectiveness of NMV-R in preventing severe illness, hospitalization, death and long-COVID in a large nationwide cohort of outpatients with COVID-19. Population-based retrospective cohort study of patients with a SARS-CoV-2 positive test or diagnosis (index) date between December 2021 and February 2023 within the National COVID Cohort Collaborative (N3C), with at least one risk factor for severe COVID-19, no evidence of contraindicated medical conditions or medication use, and no hospital or emergency department visit or death within 24 hours of eligibility. We emulated a sequence of target trials beginning on each of the first five days of diagnosis with COVID-19. We identified 921,034 eligible person-trials (each representing a patient's eligibility at a given diagnosis day across sequential emulated trials), of which 77,449 were initiators and 846,585 were non-initiators of NMV-R treatment. NMV-R Initiators were matched to non-initiators in each trial. The marginal hazard ratio between initiators and non-initiators was estimated for four acute outcomes: severe illness, hospitalization or death, hospitalization, and death; and the post-COVID condition or long COVID. Of 921,034 eligible "person-trials", 74,449 were initiators and 846,585 were non-initiators of NMV-R treatment. Pooled across trials, the hazard for severe illness (HR: 0.76, 95% CI: 0.71 to 0.81), hospitalization or death (HR: 0.50, 95% CI: 0.44 to 0.57), hospitalization (sdHR: 0.52, 95% CI: 0.46 to 0.60), death (HR: 0.33, 95% CI: 0.21 to 0.51), and long-COVID (sdHR: 0.85, 95% CI: 0.77 to 0.95) were significantly lower among NMV-R initiators compared to non-initiators. Results further indicated larger associations between NMV-R and reduced risk of both acute and post-acute outcomes with early versus delayed NMV-R treatment initiation, and among unvaccinated versus vaccinated patient subgroups. NMV-R is overall effective at preventing the risk of severe acute outcomes including hospitalization and death, as well as long COVID. Results were robust across multiple sensitivity considerations. Not applicable.

studies.title: Behind the Breathlessness: Defining Pulmonary Phenotypes in Post-COVID Syndrome.
studies.authors: Baudrexl, Josefine Christine, Alba, Jennifer Bianca Schmidt, Md, Konrad Steinestel, Gagiannis, Daniel
studies.abstract: Persistent respiratory symptoms after COVID-19 may conceal distinct pulmonary disorders despite normal routine lung function. We characterized clinical phenotypes and three-month physiological outcomes. This retrospective single-center study included all 122 eligible patients. Multimodal evaluation informed phenotype-directed management. Available paired measurements were compared with two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment across 10 parameters; a separate sensitivity analysis carried baseline values forward when follow-up was missing. Alveolitis/ILD-dominant, bronchiolitis-dominant, and asthma-dominant presentations accounted for 61 (50.0%), 47 (38.5%), and 11 (9.0%) patients; 3 (2.5%) remained unclassified. Baseline routine lung function was categorized as normal in 98 (80.3%). Median paired changes were +2 percentage points for FEV₁ (adjusted p=0.0032), +1 for FVC (p=0.0036), +2 for DLCO (p=0.0032), and -7 for RV/TLC expressed as percent predicted (p=0.0432). Paired sample sizes differed by parameter. Carrying baseline forward did not alter the signed-rank p-values. Multimodal assessment identified pulmonary phenotypes alongside modest physiological changes after treatment. These uncontrolled observations do not establish treatment efficacy or a measured quality-of-life benefit and require prospective controlled validation.

studies.title: Early feedback elicitation and downstream participation behaviours: a retrospective observational analysis of study completion and disengagement.
studies.authors: Ter Meer, Janna, Hung, Ting-Yang, Kueper, Jacqueline K, Quer, Giorgio et al.
studies.abstract: Many health research studies and clinical trials face threats to external validity and low statistical power because they are unable to recruit and retain a sufficient number of participants. Identifying study design improvements using participant feedback is an important avenue through which studies seek to address these challenges. However, the returns on this approach have been limited because experience measures are rarely linked to actual participation behaviour. We examine whether feedback collected at the beginning of a research study can provide a meaningful signal about future participation as measured by study completion, withdrawal, and communication unsubscription. We use observational data from a large health research program (N = 35,838; 77% from groups historically underrepresented in biomedical research, UBR) in which feedback was collected across the participant experience. We correlate feedback responses (e.g., indicating satisfaction with the experience) with study completion and active disengagement 6 months later and use Artificial Intelligence (AI) processing of free-text comments to surface specific topics and sentiment. Ratings given immediately after onboarding are associated with an 8.89 percentage-point (pp) higher study completion rate ('Good' vs 'Fair') and a 23.22 pp higher active disengagement rate ('Poor' vs 'Fair') within 6 months. Associations for feedback collected later are smaller (up to 4.17 pp for completion). These differences hold after adjusting for participant characteristics (age, income, educational attainment, sex at birth, UBR on race/ethnicity, and UBR on rurality). We find no statistically significant effect of the prompt itself. AI-extracted topics and sentiment agree with human reviewers 86% and 81% of the time, respectively. Early, light-touch feedback can meaningfully differentiate participants by their likelihood of completing or disengaging from a study, creating opportunities to target support and address flagged concerns while the study is still in progress. Feedback collected at the end of a study is a weaker signal of future behaviour. Our approach, including AI processing of free-text comments, is readily portable to other studies and feedback elicitations. Whether feedback-informed changes improve retention is an important question for future work. National Institutes of Health.

studies.title: Echoes of infection: viral persistence, immune activation, and histopathological changes in long COVID: a systematic review.
studies.authors: Elmahroky, Abdelrahman, Aly, Yahya, Farghaly, Aser, Abdelrasoul, Hisham et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID, or post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC), affects an estimated 10-20% of individuals following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Despite its substantial global burden, the pathophysiological mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This systematic review aimed to synthesize available evidence on viral persistence, immune activation, and histopathological changes across multiple organ systems, drawing from studies of individuals with Long COVID as well as broader post-acute cohorts, autopsy investigations, and case-based reports relevant to Long COVID pathophysiology. Following PRISMA guidelines and holding a PROSPERO registration (CRD420261403869), a systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE, and Cochrane CENTRAL. Eligible reports were stratified as (A) symptom-defined Long COVID assessed at or after 12 weeks, (B) post-acute or mixed populations without a consistently confirmed Long COVID definition or timing, (C) autopsy studies, and (D) isolated case/fetal reports. Findings were synthesized narratively by specimen, assay target, and unit of analysis. JBI checklists were used for item-level appraisal, not as certainty-of-evidence ratings. Forty-five reports were included: 16 in stratum A, 23 in stratum B, three autopsy studies, and three isolated case/fetal reports. SARS-CoV-2 genomic RNA, viral proteins, and markers compatible with recent viral activity were reported in selected tissue and blood compartments, but detection varied with population selection, timing, specimen, and assay. No included study established replication competence by recovery of infectious virus. Histopathological abnormalities included inflammatory infiltrates, fibrosis, and vascular injury; however, causal attribution to Long COVID was limited by acute disease severity, biopsy indication, comorbidity, and incomplete comparator data. A single participant total was not reported because of overlapping cohorts, repeated sampling, and outcome-specific denominators. The review supports biological heterogeneity after SARS-CoV-2 infection, including residual viral material, immune dysregulation, vascular injury, and maladaptive tissue repair. Organ-specific prevalence, a hierarchy of tissue tropism, replication-competent reservoirs, and superiority of antiviral or immunomodulatory treatment remain undefined. Standardized Long COVID definitions, representative cohorts, validated assays, appropriate comparators, and longitudinal studies linking biological markers to clinical outcomes are required.

studies.title: Astrocytes as a Convergence Point for Neuroprotection and Drug Repurposing in Long COVID Comorbidities.
studies.authors: Bezerra, Caio César Ramalho, Dias, Filipe Renato Pereira, Schmitz, Izaviany, da Silva, Amanda et al.
studies.abstract: Astrocytes are central regulators of metabolic homeostasis, redox balance, and neuroimmune signaling within the central nervous system, and accumulating evidence implicates these cells as key mediators of the neurological sequelae associated with long COVID. SARS-CoV-2 has been shown to infect neural cells, inducing substantial alterations in these regulatory parameters and promoting a sustained reactive astrocyte phenotype that compromises synaptic plasticity, blood-brain barrier integrity, and metabolic support, thereby contributing to neurometabolic and neuropsychiatric dysfunction. Despite the convergence of these findings, no review has addressed the interplay between astrocyte biology, systemic metabolic and psychiatric comorbidities, and the potential for drug repurposing within a gliopharmacological context in long COVID. In this review, we propose an astrocyte-centered model in which long COVID arises from the convergence of direct viral injury and pre-existing disorders. We then critically examine the repurposing potential of three pharmacological categories, each selected on the basis of their documented actions on astrocytic metabolic, redox, or inflammatory pathways: systemic medications already in wide clinical use for metabolic and cardiovascular indications, including metformin, angiotensin II receptor blockers, calcium-channel blockers, and statins; centrally acting agents with established or emerging use in psychiatry, such as selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors and ketamine; and the glioprotective polyphenol resveratrol. Accordingly, we delineate a translational rationale for repurposing existing therapeutics to target astrocyte-mediated pathways in long COVID. This manuscript, therefore, reinforces astrocytes as central mediators of neuroprotection and supports gliopharmacological approaches as a rational strategy to mitigate neurological dysfunction in long COVID associated with neurometabolic and neuropsychiatric comorbidities.

studies.title: Health resort-based versus home-based rehabilitation for post-COVID-19 syndrome.
studies.authors: Regazzo, Gianluca, Contessa, Paola, Passarotto, Edoardo, Coraci, Daniele et al.
studies.abstract: Post-COVID-19 syndrome, presents a significant rehabilitation challenge due to the multifaceted nature of symptoms, including dyspnea, fatigue, and cognitive dysfunction. This study aimed to compare the effect of an intensive Health Resort-based rehabilitation program versus a monitored home-based rehabilitation program in patients with Post-COVID-19 syndrome. Patients with confirmed Post-COVID-19 syndrome were assigned to either a Health Resort-based rehabilitation program ( Linear mixed effects regression model analysis revealed that both interventions improved symptoms. Statistically significant time-by-group interactions indicated that the Health Resort-based rehabilitation group achieved greater improvements compared to the home-based rehabilitation group in perceived dyspnea, bilateral hand grip strength, and anxiety. Both groups showed comparable improvements in fatigue, pain, functional limitations due to dyspnea, lower limb function, cognitive function, and quality of life, with benefits maintained during follow-up. Both Health Resort-based and home-based rehabilitation are effective modalities of care delivery for Post-COVID-19 syndrome management, where integrated and multimodal interventions are required, with the Health Resort-based rehabilitation option providing additional benefits.

studies.title: Higher incidence of paediatric autoimmune liver disease post-COVID.
studies.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
studies.authors: Warner, Suz, Mtegha, Marumbo Paul, Kostova, Mariana, Jayaprakash, Kavitha et al.
studies.abstract: A higher incidence of autoimmune conditions with greater disease severity is reported post-Coronavirus Disease (COVID). The incidence and disease severity of paediatric autoimmune liver disease (AILD) post-COVID has not been assessed. Data on children <16 years of age diagnosed with AILD between 2015 and 2024 from a United Kingdom quaternary liver specialist centre was captured. Comparison of AILD incidence and presenting clinical characteristics in pre and post-COVID pandemic time-periods were made. 199 patients were newly diagnosed with AILD within the study period (82 pre-COVID [2015-2019]; 47 autoimmune hepatitis type 1 [AIH-1], 11 AIH-2, 9 primary sclerosing cholangitis [PSC], 15 overlap/autoimmune sclerosing cholangitis [ASC], and 117 post-COVID [2020-2024]; 64 AIH-1, 10 AIH-2, 20 PSC, 23 overlap/ASC). A sharp rise in the incidence of AIH-1, PSC and overlap syndrome/ASC was observed post-COVID, being most marked in the AIH-1 cohort (p < 0.0001). Children were older at disease presentation for AIH-1, PSC and overlap/ASC compared to pre-COVID, particularly in AIH-1 (p = 0.0093). Minimal variation was observed in AIH-2 patients. Most patients presenting with AIH-1 and overlap/ASC post-COVID did not have a personal history of autoimmunity. High viral coinfection rates were observed in post-COVID AIH-1 and AIH-2 presentations. The higher incidence and older presenting age of newly diagnosed AILD patients post-COVID may have resulted from immune dysregulation in susceptible children following the sudden exposure to viral infections after long periods of social isolation, triggering the onset of autoimmunity even in individuals without an autoimmune predisposition.

studies.title: Primary cilia orchestrate the multi-organ network in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis.
studies.authors: Zhao, Yafang, Tian, Zijiao, Dou, Dou, Li, Ruoxuan et al.
studies.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is an increasingly prevalent cause of chronic liver disease and a major driver of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma worldwide. Although its pathogenesis involves complex interactions among metabolic, inflammatory, and neuroendocrine processes across multiple organs, current therapeutic strategies remain largely liver-centric and fail to address this systemic complexity. Primary cilia (PC) are evolutionarily conserved microtubule-based organelles that function as cellular sensory hubs, integrating extracellular signals and coordinating metabolic and inflammatory pathways. Emerging evidence from studies of ciliopathies, obesity, and neurodegeneration suggests that ciliary dysfunction may contribute to metabolic disorders affecting multiple organ systems. Here, we synthesize current evidence to propose a cilia-centered conceptual framework for MASH pathogenesis. We outline a dual-axis model in which PCs coordinate a horizontal metabolic axis linking the liver, gut, and pancreas to regulate glucose and lipid homeostasis, and a vertical neuro-metabolic axis connecting the brain, gut, and liver to integrate neural and endocrine signaling. Within these networks, cilia-associated pathways, including mammalian target of rapamycin, Hedgehog, Wnt/β-catenin, Notch, and transforming growth factor beta signaling, modulate key processes underlying steatosis, inflammation, and fibrogenesis. Dysfunction of PCs in hypothalamic neurons, pancreatic β-cells, intestinal stromal cells, and hepatic stellate cells may collectively amplify metabolic imbalance and inflammatory signaling, thereby promoting MASH progression. Understanding the systemic regulatory role of PC provides a unifying perspective on the multi-organ nature of MASH and highlights cilia-associated pathways as potential targets for therapeutic intervention.

studies.title: Persistent neutrophil maturation deficits associate with cognitive impairment in individuals with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19.
studies.authors: Papatheodorou, Ioanna, Lázničková, Petra, Feglarová, Tereza, Blažková, Gabriela et al.
studies.abstract: Post-COVID-19 condition, or post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), is characterized by persistent cognitive impairments and immune dysregulation. While neutrophils are critical in acute COVID-19, whether their long-term functional dysregulation contributes to PASC, remains unclear. Thus, we investigated the links between immune system changes, symptom severity and cognitive impairment in PASC. In this cross-sectional study, we enrolled 40 individuals with self-reported issues with COVID-19 recovery (PASC) and 37 fully recovered (REC) volunteers. Participants were post-infection at either TP1 (from 6 up to 18 months post-infection, 7 PASC, 20 REC) or at TP2 (from 19 up to 36 months post-infection, 33 PASC, 17 REC). We evaluated the Newcastle post-COVID-19 Syndrome Follow Up Screening (NC) scores for symptom severity, and neuropsychological tests for memory, attention, and executive function. Peripheral blood was analyzed using multicolor flow cytometry, ELISA, clustering, and multivariate regression. PASC participants in both the TP1 cohort and the TP2 cohort, demonstrated increased NC scores and significant changes in neutrophil numbers and subset composition. In the TP1 cohort, the PASC group showed an increased frequency of activated CD16 Despite limitations in cohort size, requiring validation of the associations in larger cohorts, our findings may contribute to the further understanding of PASC and future new transitional perspectives for PASC management.

studies.title: Recommendations for the primary care management of post COVID and post acute infectious syndrome: a comparative analysis of international guidelines.
studies.authors: Brand, Marlene, Bellmann-Strobl, Judith, Franke, Christiana, Scheibenbogen, Carmen et al.
studies.abstract: The medical care of people with post COVID syndrome (PCS) and other post-acute infectious syndromes (PAIS) remains a major challenge as dedicated care structures are scarce, diagnostic evaluation is often complex, and curative therapies are largely lacking. General practitioners play an essential role in initial assessment and the coordination of care and treatment. However, standardized and evidence-based recommendations specifically tailored to primary care are scarce. This study aimed to analyze and compare diagnostic and therapeutic recommendations for primary care of PCS from international guidelines. Six guidelines and recommendations were included, originating from Germany, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, the United States, the WHO, and a European scientific society. The analysis revealed considerable variation in scope, level of detail and practical applicability. Most guidelines recommend symptom-based or exclusionary diagnostic approaches. Non-pharmacological interventions such as rehabilitation, self-management and psychological support are commonly addressed. In contrast, pharmacological options are rarely specified due to limited evidence. While the importance of general practitioners is acknowledged across documents, specific support structures and implementation strategies vary. To date, structured care recommendations for patients with Long COVID and other PAIS in primary care remain limited.

studies.title: Feasibility of a community-based physical activity programme in individuals with Long Covid: insights from the Hertfordshire longitudinal observational programme.
studies.authors: Logue, M, Lyus, R, Edwards, B
studies.abstract: This study explores the feasibility of implementing and evaluating a community-based physical activity programme for individuals with Long Covid in Hertfordshire, UK. Long Covid presents unique challenges including fluctuating symptoms, post-exertional malaise and difficulties with re-engagement following symptom flare-ups. Developed collaboratively by the Herts Sports & Physical Activity Partnership and local NHS Covid Rehabilitation Services, the programme aimed to address these challenges through tailored physical activity opportunities informed by the lived experience of Long Covid. A longitudinal observational design was used to evaluate programme retention, symptom severity, health-related quality of life and physical activity levels among 62 participants over a 12-month period. Data were collected via validated self-report tools including the EQ-5D-5L, EQ-VAS, SBQ-LC and VAS pain scale. High initial engagement was observed, with 89% of participants completing the first follow-up survey and 52% remaining engaged through to follow-up 4. While average physical activity minutes remained stable, the proportion of inactive participants declined from 37% to 25%. Statistically significant improvements were observed in self-rated health (EQ-VAS), breathing difficulties, fatigue and brain fog. Weak but significant correlations were found between increased physical activity and reduced symptom severity in several domains, including mobility, self-care and musculoskeletal pain. No significant changes were observed in anxiety or depression, suggesting physical activity alone may not address the full spectrum of Long Covid symptoms. These findings demonstrate that community-based physical activity interventions are feasible for people with Long Covid, though sustained behavioural change and mental health support remain important challenges. This study contributes practical insights for service development while highlighting the need for more rigorous controlled designs and diverse sampling in future research.

studies.title: Afterword/Afterworld: Beyond Imperial Breathlessness, Toward Abolitionist Medicine.
studies.authors: Kapadia, Ronak K
studies.abstract: This afterword theorizes immunity as a governing grammar of contemporary medicine, empire, and social life. Reading across the special issue, it traces how biomedical notions of defense, juridical exemption, and political impunity converge in an immunitary paradigm that organizes breath, care, and survivability unevenly across pandemics, settler colonial violence, racial capitalism, carcerality, and climate collapse. The essay develops the concept of imperial breathlessness to name the atmospheric condition through which empire rations breathable life, from COVID-19 triage and Long COVID abandonment to Gaza, prisons, policing, and ecological catastrophe. Against immunity's fantasies of autonomy, purity, and self-protection, it turns to disability justice, abolitionist medicine, infectious aesthetics, and queer/crip practices of mutual aid as fugitive infrastructures of collective survival. The afterword concludes by imagining afterworlds of care: unfinished, insurgent forms of shared respiration that move beyond immunitary enclosure toward the downward redistribution of breath and breathing in common.

This response is a precursor to cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and end-stage liver failure, which have a substantial global health burden and limited therapeutic options. studies.title: Ginseng Guben Oral Liquid, a Chinese patent medicine, for post-COVID-19 fatigue: A multicenter randomized controlled trial.
studies.authors: Dai, Liang, Kuah, Xiu Juan, Liu, Zhi-Dong, Hua, Hai-Bing et al.
studies.abstract: Fatigue is a prevalent and debilitating symptom in patients with post-COVID-19 condition, yet effective pharmacological interventions remain limited. Ginseng Guben Oral Liquid (RSGB), a modern patented Chinese herbal formula, is clinically used to treat fatigue associated with qi and yin deficiency, a pattern relevant to post-COVID-19 fatigue. However, high-quality evidence from randomized controlled trials is lacking. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of RSGB in patients with post-COVID-19 fatigue. This study was a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. A total of 264 eligible participants with post-COVID-19 fatigue and traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) syndrome of qi and yin deficiency were enrolled from several clinical centers and randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either RSGB or a matched placebo (10 mL, twice daily) for 8 weeks, followed by a 4-week follow-up. The primary outcome was the change in points from baseline in the Chalder Fatigue Questionnaire (CFQ) score at week 8. Secondary outcomes included quality of life, TCM syndrome score, inflammatory markers and immune cell subsets. In the modified intention-to-treat population, no significant difference in the mean reduction in CFQ scores was observed between the RSGB and placebo groups (-16.0 ± 5.7 vs -15.4 ± 5.7, P = 0.404). No significant differences were observed in secondary outcomes. In a pre-specified exploratory subgroup analysis of participants with severe baseline fatigue (CFQ ≥ 22, n = 90), the results of the group treated with RSGB showed a greater reduction in CFQ scores compared to the placebo (-20.7 ± 5.6 vs -17.8 ± 6.0, P = 0.027), particularly in the domain of physical fatigue. The incidence of adverse events was comparable between groups, with no serious adverse events reported. RSGB did not demonstrate a significant overall benefit over placebo in the general post-COVID-19 fatigue. The potential signal of benefit observed in the severe fatigue subgroup requires prospective validation in trials specifically designed for this population. These findings highlight symptom severity as a factor for further research in stratified management approaches. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2300069518). studies.title: Liver-related biochemical abnormalities and coagulation alterations in long COVID: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
studies.journal: The American journal of the medical sciences
studies.authors: Almulla, Abbas F, Thipakorn, Yanin, Zhang, Yingqian, Maes, Michael
studies.abstract: This meta-analysis aimed to compare liver-related biochemical and coagulation biomarkers between individuals with Long COVID (LC) and controls. A search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Google Scholar, SciFinder, and Scopus was conducted from database inception to September 30, 2024. Sixty-one eligible studies, including 7172 participants, with 3404 individuals with LC and 3768 controls were identified. Among the liver-related biochemical markers, LC was associated with significantly higher alanine aminotransferase (ALT; SMD = 0.398; 95% CI: 0.118; 0.677), aspartate aminotransferase (AST; SMD = 0.352; 95% CI: 0.068; 0.637), and gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT; SMD = 0.969; 95% CI: 0.194; 1.745) along with no significant changes in alkaline phosphatase and bilirubin. The composite liver biomarker index, based on those five markers was significantly higher among individuals with LC compared with controls, with a small effect size (SMD = 0.381; 95% CI: 0.149; 0.613). Among the complementary systemic and coagulation-related outcomes, lactate dehydrogenase activity (LDH; SMD = 0.489; 95% CI: 0.175; 0.802), prothrombin time (PT, SMD = 0.633; 95% CI: 0.077; 1.189), ferritin (SMD = 0.437; 95% CI: 0.069; 0.805), and D-dimer (SMD = 0.359; 95% CI: 0.144; 0.573) were significantly increased, whereas total protein was significantly decreased (SMD = -0.326; 95% CI: -0.631; -0.021). The present meta-analysis indicates that LC is associated with persistent abnormalities in several liver-related biochemical markers and coagulation-related outcomes. Further longitudinal studies are required to determine their clinical significance and long-term consequences.

studies.title: Psychosocial impacts of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19: insights from a longitudinal cohort.
studies.authors: Vallejos, Gerome, Kim, Carla Y, Alviz, Luisa F, Diaz-Ariza, Alexandra et al.
studies.abstract: To characterize subjective stress in a previously hospitalized Neuropsychiatric Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19 (NP-PASC) cohort in New York City by examining its distribution, patterns, and associations with psychosocial and cognitive measures. This longitudinal study conducted a 3-4 year follow-up of moderate to severe COVID-19 survivors with NP-PASC, using the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS), Urban Life Stress Scale (ULSS), and Everyday Discrimination Scale (EDS) to assess chronic stress. Associations with DSM-5 symptom domains, PSQI, UCLA Loneliness, ECog, and AD8 were analyzed using descriptive statistics, t-tests, ANOVA, chi-squared tests, and multivariate linear regression (p < 0.05). K-means clustering on standardized PSS scores identified PSS score strata (low, intermediate, high). All analyses were conducted in R version 4.3.2. Among 87 participants (mean age = 54, SD = 14), mean PSS scores for the low, intermediate, and high stress clusters were 7.08, 16.8, and 26.7, respectively. Higher perceived stress was associated with loneliness (β = 0.20, p < 0.001) and poor sleep (β = 0.34, p = 0.05). PSS scores increased by 2.07 points over time (p = 0.013), with greater increases among Hispanic (3.88, p = 0.026) and English-speaking (3.33, p = 0.008) participants. ULSS scores were higher among Spanish speakers (6.43, p = 0.017) and Hispanic/Other participants (9.5 vs. Black, p = 0.009). Discrimination experiences varied significantly by race, ethnicity, and language. Findings underscore the importance of integrating culturally sensitive, context-informed stress assessments into NP-PASC care to identify at-risk individuals and support recovery.

studies.title: Visual-verbal scanning and attention performance in individuals with long COVID-19-related dysautonomia.
studies.authors: González-Vides, Leonela, García-Velasco, Marta Alberquilla, Ruiz-Pomeda, Alicia, Hernández-Verdejo, Jose Luis et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID-19-related dysautonomia is associated with persistent cognitive and visual complaints, but brief clinically feasible tools for characterizing visual-attentional performance are needed. In this case-control study, 48 individuals with long COVID-19-related dysautonomia and 30 healthy controls completed the Modified Adult Developmental Eye Movement Test (ADEM-d), a timed visual-verbal reading/scanning task that requires sequential saccadic deployment, and the Continuous Visual Attention Test (CVAT). Compared with controls, the study group showed longer adjusted horizontal (median 73.63 vs. 54.69 s), vertical (66.35 vs. 50.66 s), and distractor (83.97 vs. 64.55 s) reading times (all Holm-adjusted p < 0.001; rank-biserial r = 0.58-0.60), whereas the horizontal/vertical ratio did not differ significantly (p = 0.108). On the CVAT, the study group showed longer reaction time (378.5 vs. 320.0 ms; Holm-adjusted p < 0.001), greater reaction-time variability (96.0 vs. 62.5 ms; p = 0.001), and more omission errors (p = 0.028). Across the full sample, distractor-condition ADEM-d time was positively associated with omission errors, reaction time, and reaction-time variability (Spearman rho = 0.55-0.58; all p < 0.001). These findings indicate altered functional visual-verbal scanning and visual-attentional performance in this cohort. Because the ADEM-d does not directly record eye movements, the results do not demonstrate a primary saccadic motor deficit; additionally, the absence of a long-COVID group without dysautonomia prevents attribution of the findings specifically to dysautonomia. The ADEM-d and CVAT may nevertheless provide brief screening information to identify individuals who require more detailed visual, oculomotor, or neuropsychological assessment.

studies.title: Low-dose aripiprazole for long COVID symptom management: A retrospective observational study.
studies.authors: Cui, Jason Lunzhe, Kalaycioglu, Muge, Ricciardiello Mejia, Giorgio Camillo, Tian, Lu et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID (LC) is defined as the persistence of new or worsened symptoms for 3 or more months following acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, affecting multiple organ systems. Currently, there are no approved drugs for treating LC. We reported the effect of low-dose Aripiprazole (LDA) on the management of LC symptoms in a retrospective study. A retrospective study was done using electronic health records from 50 adult patients from the Stanford LC clinic with a history of SARS-CoV-2 and subsequent LC who received LDA between 5/2021 and 10/2023. LDA was prescribed with dose titration (0.1-2.0 mg oral daily). The assessment include 29 symptoms, (ii) severity of each symptom on the Likert-scale 1 (mild) to 5 (very severe), and (iii) the Functional Status Scale (FSS) from asymptomatic (level I), symptomatic without limitations (level II), symptomatic with reduced daily activity (level III), symptomatic with a struggle to perform daily activities (level IV), or incapacitated and bedridden (level V). An improvement was defined as a reduction in the ordinal scale (V, IV, III, II, and I) from higher to lower before and after exposure to LDA. A composite score of the severity of the seven most common symptoms (headache, fatigue, brain fog, unrefreshing sleep, sleep difficulty, post-exertional malaise, and lightheadedness) was calculated to assess the effect of LDA pre- and post-treatment, using Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Tests. Within the cohort of 50 patients, the median patient age was 46.5 years, 62% were female, and the mean body mass index (BMI) was 27.5 kg/m In our cohort study, LDA was associated with improved FSS. These retrospective observational results suggest that LDA warrants further investigation in a randomized controlled trial as a therapeutic option for LC. Exploring the mechanism of action for LDA in LC may also provide new insights into pathogenesis.

studies.title: Predictors of Long COVID in Adults With Untreated Mild-to-Moderate Coronavirus Disease 2019.
studies.authors: Evering, Teresa H, Saha, Pooja T, Moser, Carlee, Jilg, Nikolaus et al.
studies.abstract: We evaluated risk factors for long COVID (LC) in the ACTIV-2/A5401 trial, with a focus on understanding the impact of sex. Findings were analyzed in nonhospitalized adults with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) receiving placebo within 10 days of symptoms. LC was defined as self-reporting COVID-19-related symptoms at study week 24 in a diary. Demographics and clinical variables, nasal viral RNA (vRNA), and inflammatory/coagulation markers were evaluated as predictors of LC, using modified Poisson regression models. Among 545 participants enrolled in January-August 2021 with a week 24 diary, the median age at entry was 44 years, 53% were female, 13% Black, 53% Hispanic/Latino, 83% US enrolled, 15% vaccinated, and 52% severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) seropositive. Seventy-four (14%) had LC (19% of female and 7% of male participants). Female sex was strongly associated with LC (adjusted risk ratio, 2.64 [95% confidence interval, 1.58-4.42]). Other predictors included US enrollment, higher total symptom score at entry, presence of symptoms at the end of the acute period (days 22-28), 28-day area under the curve of vRNA levels, and higher day 28 C-reactive protein and fibrinogen. The effect of sex persisted with adjustment for the other variables, and associations with symptoms and fibrinogen level varied by sex. In untreated adults with COVID-19, female sex, US enrollment, symptom and vRNA burden, and inflammatory/coagulation measures were associated with increased LC risk, with some associations varying by sex. The association with female sex was not significantly attenuated by adjustment for the assessed biomarkers. These data support sex-stratified investigations of LC, as well as a potential role of thromboinflammation. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04518410.

studies.title: Associations between substance use and symptomatic Long COVID in the Researching COVID to Enhance Recovery (RECOVER)-adult cohort study.
studies.authors: Okafor, Chukwuemeka N, Peterson, Ryan, Nepple, Cecilia, Jolley, Sarah et al.
studies.abstract: To determine whether frequency of tobacco, cannabis and binge alcohol use in the 12 months prior to SARS-CoV-2 test result or COVID-19 symptom onset is associated with (1) presence of symptomatic Long COVID at study entry and (2) development of symptomatic Long COVID over 12 months of follow-up, among those without Long COVID at study entry. Prospective cohort study with cross-sectional and longitudinal components. Multi-site study conducted across 83 clinical sites in the United States. A total of 9477 adults enrolled between October 2021 and July 2024 (median age 43 years; 74% female). Self-reported frequency of tobacco product, cannabis and binge alcohol use in the 12 months prior to SARS-CoV-2 test infection (never, monthly or less, weekly or none). Symptomatic Long COVID was defined using the Researching COVID to Enhance Recovery (RECOVER)-Adult Long COVID Research Index, with scores ≥ 11 classified as symptomatic Long COVID and lower scores classified as indeterminate. Covariates included sociodemographic characteristics, clinical comorbidities and COVID-19 related factors. At study entry 20% of participants met criteria for symptomatic Long COVID. In the 12 months preceding infection, 14%, 21% and 38% reported any tobacco product, cannabis or binge alcohol use. At study entry, compared with no use, weekly or more tobacco use was associated with higher odds of symptomatic Long COVID [adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 1.37, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.13-1.67]; weekly or more cannabis use was associated with higher odds of symptomatic Long COVID (aOR = 1.23, 95% CI = 1.00-1.52); and weekly or more binge alcohol use was associated with lower odds (aOR = 0.73, 95% CI = 0.58-0.91) of symptomatic Long COVID. Monthly or less use of any substance was not associated with symptomatic Long COVID at study entry. Among participants without symptomatic Long COVID at study entry, weekly or more tobacco use, compared with no use, was associated with higher odds of developing symptomatic Long COVID over 12 months of follow-up (aOR = 1.29, 95% CI = 1.03-1.62). Neither cannabis nor binge alcohol use was statistically significantly associated with symptomatic Long COVID at 12-month follow-up. Among adult participants of the Researching COVID to Enhance Recovery (RECOVER) study, weekly or more tobacco use in the 12 months prior to SARS-CoV-2 infection was associated with higher odds of symptomatic Long COVID at study entry and at 12 months among participants who did not meet criteria for symptomatic Long COVID at study entry. Weekly or more cannabis use was associated with higher odds of symptomatic Long COVID at study entry and was not associated with symptomatic Long COVID at 12 months. Weekly or more binge alcohol use was associated with lower odds of symptomatic Long COVID at study entry and was not associated with symptomatic Long COVID at 12 months.

studies.title: Through the Long COVID Looking-Glass: An Unremitting Conundrum of Mitochondria?
studies.authors: Kononova, Svetlana, Bobkova, Natalia, Leonov, Sergey, Sukhikh, Gennadiy
studies.abstract: Plentiful data indicate a high post-COVID risk of developing pathologies that are long-term and result from disruption of multiple cellular processes. The significance of this data becomes increasingly clear as it links the pandemic's effects to enduring health problems which could affect millions. These conditions are usually caused by different problems with mitochondria. These problems can include less efficient energy production and increased removal of damaged cells, showing how complex cell health is. Having other health problems such as high blood pressure, type 2 diabetes, brain diseases, and cancer related to renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) imbalance worsened COVID-19 and its lasting effects. This highlights the importance of focused treatments for these at-risk groups. This review seeks to evaluate the information on this issue, carefully studying the features and symptoms often associated with mitochondrial disorders. What happens next in the pandemic is still to be seen, but we know there is much to learn. It is important to lessen the effects of the pandemic on people with comorbidities as much as possible.

studies.title: Systemic influences on blood-brain barrier integrity - narrative review of insights from MRI.
studies.authors: Verstappen, Damon, de Jong, Joost J A, Staals, Julie, Jansen, Jacobus F A et al.
studies.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) is vital for protecting the vulnerable neuronal microenvironment from harmful biomolecules. MRI is increasingly used to assess in vivo BBB integrity in various brain disorders. Thus far, extracerebral conditions that perturb the BBB via systemic pathways have received little attention. This narrative review synthesizes the available evidence for these extracerebral and systemic effects, focusing on human in vivo MRI measurements of BBB permeability. The most direct reproducible human evidence of BBB impairment was found in hypertension. Moderate evidence supports BBB involvement in systemic lupus erythematosus and long COVID. There is additionally suggestive evidence for an association with Sjögren's syndrome, HIV infection, diabetes, cardiac surgery (transient), and after pre-eclampsia. Evidence for BBB disruption is inconclusive for conditions like obstructive sleep apnea, sepsis, hyperlipidemia, obesity, alcohol abuse, and for smoking. In general, systemic inflammation emerges as a common mechanistic pathway that leads to BBB disruption and represents a target with therapeutic potential. Inflammation is amplified by a vicious cycle in which endothelial dysfunction and oxidative/metabolic stress further reinforce inflammatory signaling. Angiogenic factors also likely contribute in a subset of conditions. Heterogeneity in imaging and modeling methods and probed BBB transport pathways limits cross-study comparability. Furthermore, inherent confounding factors limit the power to detect subtle effects. Large-scale DCE-MRI studies are needed to be able to robustly map the influence of various extracerebral conditions on BBB integrity.

studies.title: Personalized cognitive and physical Telerehabilitation in post-COVID-19 condition and ME/CFS: A pilot randomized controlled trial.
studies.authors: Azcue, N, Barranco-Cano, C, Tijero-Merino, B, Acera, M et al.
studies.abstract: Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) and post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) share fatigue, post-exertional symptom exacerbation, and cognitive impairment. To explore preliminary effects and feasibility of personalized telerehabilitation in PCC and ME/CFS. This pilot randomized controlled trial analyzed 79 participants with baseline and 16-week assessments: 46 intervention and 33 standard-care controls. Individualized asynchronous cognitive and motor training was prescribed four times weekly and adapted weekly. Outcomes included neuropsychological performance, self-reported symptoms, and six-minute walk test performance. Feasibility measures included platform-recorded adherence and System Usability Scale (SUS) scores. Between-group change comparisons and domain-level Time × Group interactions were not significant after false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Within-intervention improvements in sustained attention and semantic verbal fluency remained significant after FDR correction (both pFDR = 0.028). Exploratory principal component analysis identified PC1, explaining 27.2% of cognitive change variance. Covariate-adjusted regressions showed higher PC1 scores in intervention participants (β = 0.715, p = 0.043) and a positive association with motor adherence within this group (β = 0.089, p = 0.005); these p-values were not corrected for multiple comparisons. Median motor and cognitive adherence were 99.75% and 100.00%, respectively; median SUS was 77.5. Recorded adherence and usability provided preliminary support for feasibility under individualized clinical support, whose contact intensity was not systematically recorded. Domain-level analyses did not establish differential cognitive benefit after FDR correction. Exploratory PCA findings require confirmation in larger, adequately powered trials.
